verifiedUsageBaseline.source: Google Cloud Billing UI, read by the operator; usage before the Cloud SQL migration, not a monthly invoice or new-runtime cost measurement

assumptions: User selected staging Cloud SQL; production remains on its existing VM and database.
730 billing hours, zonal PostgreSQL17 g1-small, 50GiB SSD. No HA, PITR, managed full backups or commitment discounts.
Public request path uses at most three separate 1vCPU/512MiB services. Low/high quantities model 5/20 active hours for each; broker usage and cold starts are included in the reserve.
Cloud Run services have min0/max1. Request-based billing; no continuously running provider scheduler.
Monthly heavy import uses 2vCPU/8GiB for 8/24 hours. A persistent total three-attempt budget caps heavy work at3x8h per UTC month; daily due checks do not import when not due.

Maintenance quantities use a30-day month. Replace the former daily cleanup minimum30x60s (0.5vCPUh/0.25GiBh) inside the combined maintenance lines with720 hourly executions: low60s minimum billing (12vCPUh/6GiBh), high300s application deadline (60vCPUh/30GiBh). The previous2vCPUh/1GiBh high-scenario maintenance allowance remains; the10percent reserve covers startup/shutdown variation. Exact additional net cost is0.692208-3.581424EUR before reserve/tax.

The existing cleanup job runs hourly, first bounded expired availability retention (up to64 snapshot targets and120s), then up to32x1000 derived search rows. One583004-row replacement needs approximately19 successful search-cleanup invocations. Large live snapshots may require multiple runs; measure duration/backlog, because runs over60s increase billed CPU/memory. Hourly support purge preserves the existing deletion deadline.
Daily backups have a3600-second ceiling and zero platform retries. Failed backups require attention; they do not silently enable report-containing managed backups.

Backup and cache are separate UBLA/PAP buckets. Model40-55GiB combined storage, finite lifecycle, no redundant object versioning/soft-delete for public reproducible cache.30GiB filtered-backup storage alone costs0.528EUR/month.
Application corpus measured22.78GiB and cache0.883GiB before migration.50GiB SQL needs real shadow-import/storage and g1-small-memory validation.
GCP ingress for public provider downloads is not internet egress. CPU/download time, outbound responses and cross-region registry transfer are modeled separately.
Supplemental USD list rates use0.88EUR/USD as a planning conversion; SKU-marked rates came from the live EUR public catalog. No free quota or billing credits assumed.
No load balancer, NAT gateway or proxy VM. Staging custom domain uses the regional preview domain mapping; its preview constraints must be accepted.
10percent reserve does not bound the invoice. Resource caps limit concurrency/durations, not traffic volume, storage growth or all transfer charges.
The old staging VM and retained disks must be retired only after acceptance; overlap and one-time seed/restore costs are additional, not included in steady state.
No automatic SQL resize. A temporary larger DB for import is a separate reviewed cost/change; g1-small performance is not established by this price model.
measurementGates: Verify first authenticated search, cold start and concurrent requests on g1-small; record aggregate p95, connection count, CPU/RAM and timeouts.
Measure one full charging+food import before relying on the8h attempt limit, including peak SQL disk usage and provider/cache bytes.
Validate filtered backup restore, hourly purge and hourly bounded cleanup before enabling schedules; measure expired-live backlog and cleanup execution above the60s billing floor.
Compare actual per-service billing after at least48hours and after the first monthly import; billing export can lag24hours or longer.
At projected52EUR net reassess activity/storage assumptions; before projected68.94EUR net, the verified comparable baseline, require owner decision. Budget alerts do not stop spend.
